newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - MAM new business stays strong.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - MAM new business stays strong.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management Group Plc has seen continued strong growth in new business since the end of March following a record full year performance, chairman Hugh Stevenson said.
In an interview following the release of annual results, Stevenson said the strong new business trend had continued into the current year.
The group pulled in a record 5.3 billion sterling in net new business in the year, and 3.3 billion in the second half alone. The previous full year record was 3.6 billion.
Stevenson said the strong new business figure had been buoyed by the UK and Japan in particular, and MAM had won a considerable number of mandates in the year.
Funds under management rose to 89.7 billion stg from 81 billion.

MAM reported a rise in pre-tax profits to 171.3 million stg against 140.4 million previously, which was in line with expectations. It announced a higher than expected dividend totalling 45 pence against expectations of between 41 and 42 pence.
Stevenson said the higher dividend reflected the group's push for a more liberal distribution policy.

But he said MAM's strong balance sheet, supported by a 250 million sterling loan facility it took out earlier this year, represented an appropriate level of capital and liquidity and MAM had no intention of drawing down capital through a distribution to shareholders.
Although it had not ruled out acquisitions to build its business, this would not be done without considering value for shareholders, he said.

Stevenson said the group had done well so far by growing organically. In the U.S, MAM added $1 billion in new assets with major plan sponsors, reflecting success in obtaining international specialist mandates.
The international business remained the faster growth area for MAM, but he said the UK market was not static, especially in defined contribution area.

"Clearly the core of the business was UK institutional mandates but the market for fund management generally is so large and so diverse that it is a question of seeing where the real opportunities are and going for them, and clearly that includes both institutional and retail business."
A MAM spokesman said the areas that the group was looking to build internationally included Japan, the U.S., Germany, Australia and the Netherlands.
Stevenson said it was too early to comment on possible changes by the new Labour government to Advance Corporation Tax (ACT), which pension funds have warned could undermine the industry.
"Obviously anyone can work out the arithmetic...but I think it is too early to comment until we know what the budget next month is going to hold," he said.
